chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Do not give anyone less than a head (of grain)." And it has been narrated that it is permissible to distribute it in parts, [it] narrated.

key_terms.تَفْرِيقِ: Distribution; splitting or dividing the amount.
key_terms.جَوَازُ: Permissibility; the legal ruling that an action is allowed.
key_terms.رَأْسٍ: A head; a specific unit of measurement for grain (approx. 750g-1kg) used in calculating minimum alms.

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of fitrah to give to a poor person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to ensure the dignity of the recipient by preventing the distribution of negligible amounts that might be considered insulting. The mention of the permissibility of splitting the 'head' (a specific weight of grain, typically wheat or barley) reflects the practical flexibility in Zakat al-Fitr distribution, allowing donors to meet the minimum threshold even if they lack the full measure at once. This highlights the Shia emphasis on both the sufficiency of the gift and the ease of fulfilling the obligation.
